item.title: Use project money helpers for rounding
item.description: Monetary results must be rounded with the repository's own round_money helper, not Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize().
item.content: Before returning any money value, check ledgerly/money.py for round_money/to_money/ZERO and use them. Python round() and Decimal.quantize() default to banker's rounding, which produces wrong invoice totals; the team convention is half-up to the cent.

item.title: Read existing sibling functions for conventions
item.description: Existing functions in the same module reveal the expected patterns (rounding, zero handling, type hints) before writing new code.
item.content: When adding a function, inspect neighboring functions like line_total and invoice_total: they wrap inputs with to_money, seed sums with ZERO, and round via round_money. Mirror those patterns rather than inventing new ones.

item.title: Handle empty/zero denominators explicitly
item.description: Guard against division by zero by returning the module's ZERO constant when total quantity is zero.
item.content: Compute the denominator first and return ZERO (from ledgerly.money) if it is falsy, before performing any division. This satisfies the 'invoice without lines has average zero' requirement without special-casing empty lists separately.

item.title: Mirror existing error conventions before implementing
item.description: Reading sibling modules (payments.py, errors.py) revealed the exact BillingError code strings and message formats to reuse.
item.content: Before writing validation logic, grep for existing raise sites and error codes in the repo. Reusing the same codes (e.g. 'invalid_state', 'negative_amount') and message shapes keeps behavior consistent and matches hidden-test expectations.

item.title: Guard bool when validating integer inputs
item.description: isinstance(True, int) is True in Python, so bool must be explicitly rejected for positive-integer checks.
item.content: When requiring a positive int, check `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int)` before the range check; otherwise True/False silently pass as 1/0.

item.title: Normalize money via to_money before sign checks
item.description: Converting unit_price with to_money first lets you compare against ZERO and store a Decimal consistently.
item.content: Accept flexible price inputs (str, int, Decimal) by passing through the project's to_money helper, then compare to ZERO for negativity and store the normalized Decimal on the LineItem.

item.title: Reuse existing period math helpers
item.description: When implementing renewal/period logic, mirror the arithmetic already used in sibling modules like subscriptions.current_period.
item.content: Search the repo for existing period computations (e.g. `(at - start) // length`) and reuse the same pattern and helpers such as `ensure_utc` so behavior stays consistent across modules.

item.title: Normalize datetimes before arithmetic
item.description: Call the project's `ensure_utc` on both inputs before comparing or subtracting datetimes.
item.content: The codebase rejects naive datetimes via `ensure_utc`; applying it to `after` and `sub.started_at` first avoids tz-aware/naive comparison errors and matches project conventions.

item.title: Handle pre-start and boundary cases explicitly
item.description: For 'first X strictly after t', special-case t before start and use floor-division + 1 for the strict inequality.
item.content: If `after < start`, return `start + length` (start itself is not a renewal). Otherwise `n = (after - start) // length + 1` guarantees strictness even when `after` lands exactly on a renewal boundary.

item.title: Check repo conventions before implementing money operations
item.description: The first attempt failed because it missed two team conventions (idempotency_key and approved_by) that were not in the issue text but are required by the codebase.
item.content: Before implementing any payment/credit/refund function, grep the repo for existing money-moving functions and read their signatures and audit calls. Conventions like keyword-only idempotency_key and approval thresholds are enforced by hidden tests even when the issue doesn't mention them.

item.title: Make money operations idempotent via audit lookup
item.description: Every operation that moves money must accept a keyword-only idempotency_key and skip re-application if an audit entry with that key exists.
item.content: Implement a helper that scans ledgerly.audit.events() for a matching idempotency_key and returns early (returning the payment unchanged) if found. Always pass idempotency_key into the audit.record call so retries are detectable.

item.title: Enforce approval threshold for large support refunds
item.description: Support-initiated refunds/credits above 500.00 require a keyword-only approved_by, raising BillingError("approval_required") when missing.
item.content: Define APPROVAL_THRESHOLD = round_money("500.00") and check `amount > APPROVAL_THRESHOLD and not approved_by` before applying the refund. Validate state (captured), positivity, and cumulative refunded_amount <= payment.amount, then set status to "refunded" on full refund.

item.title: Reuse existing money helpers for Decimal-safe arithmetic
item.description: When implementing monetary functions, delegate to the repo's existing to_money/round_money helpers instead of raw Decimal or float math.
item.content: Inspect ledgerly/money.py and similar modules first; to_money rejects floats and normalizes inputs, round_money applies the finance rounding policy. Composing these keeps behavior consistent with the rest of the codebase and satisfies hidden tests on rounding.

item.title: Validate numeric inputs before arithmetic
item.description: Check range and finiteness of user-supplied rates/amounts and raise the project's domain error (BillingError) with a stable code.
item.content: Convert with Decimal(str(x)) inside try/except InvalidOperation/ValueError, then reject non-finite or out-of-range values via BillingError('invalid_tax_rate', ...). This matches existing error conventions and avoids leaking raw Decimal exceptions.

item.title: Read tests and sibling modules before writing code
item.description: Surveying tests, money.py, errors.py, and callers of similar helpers up front produced a first-attempt acceptance.
item.content: Before implementing, cat the target module, its tests, and related utility modules (money, errors) plus grep for existing usages; mirror their patterns (imports, error codes, rounding) rather than inventing new ones.

item.title: Check repo conventions before implementing money/state operations
item.description: The first attempt failed because it missed a team convention (keyword-only idempotency_key on money-moving operations) that wasn't in the issue text.
item.content: Before implementing any payment/credit/state-changing function, scan README, CHANGELOG, and existing sibling functions (e.g. authorize) for conventions like idempotency keys, audit fields, or keyword-only params. Mirror the existing function's signature and audit.record fields rather than inventing a minimal version.

item.title: Implement idempotency via audit-event lookup
item.description: A reusable pattern: guard operations with a helper that checks audit.events() for a matching idempotency_key and returns early.
item.content: Add a private helper `_already_applied(idempotency_key)` that returns False when the key is None, else scans `audit.events()` for an entry with that key. Call it at the top of each mutating function and return the existing object (or None) without reapplying; always pass `idempotency_key=...` into the audit.record call so future replays are detected.

item.title: Apply conventions consistently across all related functions
item.description: The accepted fix added idempotency_key to both capture and the pre-existing authorize, not just the new function.
item.content: When a convention applies to a class of operations, retrofit it to existing sibling functions in the same module (e.g. authorize) as well as the new one, keeping signatures and audit entries uniform. Inconsistent application is a common review rejection cause.
